message:
feat(water): yachts in the marinas, houseboats on their registered berths

The canal moorings refuse wide water on purpose, so a harbour basin stood
empty: the Oosterhaven, full of yachts in the aerial photo, had none, and
the 753 houseboat berths the BAG registers in Groningen drew nothing at all —
they reached the client only for the address readout.

- Yachts (`FurnitureKind::Yacht`, white hull and cabin, a mast) moor
  alongside OSM's jetties (`pier_lines`, `pier_polygons`, 63 around
  Groningen) and along the quays of any basin a jetty stands in, within
  120 m of it, one per 14 m, kept only where the whole hull is over water and
  off every jetty, 7 m apart, and clear of a registered berth.
- Houseboats (`FurnitureKind::Houseboat`) stand on every registered berth,
  lying along the nearest bank. Where the register's own building stands on
  the berth — a woonark 3DBAG already models — only the hull is drawn under
  it (`FurnitureInstance::hull_only`), or the house was a box inside a box.
- Both float like the canal boats. Where no water level is registered they
  take the level the water is drawn at (the median of its outline, as
  `water_surface` does) rather than the carve's floor.

`FurnitureMask` is a u32 now: these made seventeen forms. Both slugs join
the placeholder vocabulary, in core and in the web UI's copy.

feat(chats): send pictures in private chats, end to end encrypted

A person can send a photo or image from the device, or a snapshot of the
map as they see it, into a private chat; the bot can send what its avatar
sees (`send_picture`) and look at what it is sent (`see_picture`).

A private chat's log refuses entries over 64 KB so it cannot become a
file store, so a picture travels in two halves. The sender shrinks it to
the place-photo size, encrypts it with ChaCha20-Poly1305 under a random
key made for it alone (`cartopolis_e2ee::seal_attachment`, on the
RustCrypto provider MLS already uses, so no new dependency and no C), and
uploads the ciphertext to a new `/api/pictures` store keyed by hash. Only
then does it send `Payload::Picture` with the hash and the key, sealed
like every other message. The server holds ciphertext it cannot open,
checks only size (4 MB) and a per-account rate (120/h), and keeps no
row. `Payload` is append-only and `Picture` is its sixth variant, so
there is no protocol revision: an older app shows "can't display".

Every chat picture is drawn as a Polaroid: warm white paper, a deep
bottom edge with the caption, a soft shadow. A snapshot reuses the dev
panel's chrome-free screenshot path and hands the raw pixels to a
worker to encode.

Also fixed: a place card sent to the bot arrived as its caption alone,
"a place" for an unnamed one, so the bot told jeroen nothing had come.
`read_chat` now prints a card's coordinates, and `me`, `read_chat` and
`wait` report anybody sharing their live location.

Verified between two headless clients on a local simulator: contact
request, accept, `send_picture`, `read_chat`, `see_picture` returned the
picture. The Polaroid was checked in a `--ui chatthread` capture with a
demo picture; neither the picker nor the snapshot button has been
pressed on a device.

feat(mcp): let the bot know where it is, keep places and notes, and sit down

The Deck bot could act but could not perceive without a picture, the most
expensive thing it can ask for, and nothing it learned outlived a
conversation. Sixteen tools close most of that:

- look_around: the surroundings in words, from what is already loaded for
  the person at the keyboard (WorldPlaces, BuildingFacts, the prims): the
  address or building it is in, people, objects and which are scripted,
  named places, street furniture by kind, and buildings with the register's
  use, year and monument status, each with distance and compass direction.
- look: a picture through the avatar's own eyes, captured in place in the
  first-person camera, so it neither teleports nor stands a seated avatar
  up. Seated, it turns the head rather than the body.
- find_place (the address bar's Nominatim lookup, biased to the avatar),
  save_place / my_places / forget_place, and a `place` name on walk_to and
  teleport.
- wait: a long poll on chat, arrivals, calls, contact requests, script
  output and the end of a walk.
- follow, sit / stand, interact (what E does, walking there first), face,
  and edit_object (an UpdatePrim carrying the object's whole state, as the
  gizmo sends, with only the named fields changed).
- remember / recall / forget_note: a notebook per account and server in the
  Data namespace beside the build list.
- me now gives the time, the sun and the weather.

A parked read_chat or wait no longer keeps a headless client at the full
frame rate: that is how a bot sits in a conversation, and counting it
would undo the idle rate for exactly the stretch it is for.
Nor does it idle while any streamer is still busy: every streamer is
bounded per frame, so at 2 Hz the Deck bot found no shops or benches for
minutes after starting, while the buildings, which stream without a
frame cap, were already there.

An arrival now allows for the coming frame's step and strolls the last
four metres. The sim moves the avatar on the last wish until the next
intent; on this container's 3 s frames that walked a test bot 5 m past
the box it was going to press.

Avatar appearance is not on the wire, so changing the bot's outfit was
left out: nobody else would see it.

perf(mcp): a headless client idles at 2 Hz between calls

The Deck's bot drew the whole city into an offscreen image at the run
loop's 30 Hz while waiting for a call nobody had made, holding the
Deck's GPU at 99% busy and most of a core. A headless MCP client now
stretches its frame to half a second whenever nothing is in flight: no
capture in progress, no `view` waiting, no walk and no pending line or
build. Each of those runs at the full rate, so every tool behaves as
before, and a call arriving mid-sleep waits at most 0.5 s.

Not drawing at all while idle was tried first. Bevy 0.19 panics on the
next frame when the only camera goes inactive: bevy_pbr's
prepare_atmosphere_probe_bind_groups unwraps an empty transform buffer,
and its types are private, so there is nothing to switch off instead.

On lavapipe this changes nothing (an idle frame there already takes
1.3 s), so it was measured on the Deck bot itself.

fix(map): what a pass over Groningen against the aerial photo found

A QA sweep at 6 m to 4 km, every view beside PDOK's aerial photograph of the
same ground, found the map and the place disagreeing in these ways.

- The basemap image is the 3D ground's picture now. Above FLAT_GROUND_OFF_M
  it replaces the meshes, and it was painted from OSM alone: the Grote Markt
  went from brick to white and every street from paving to a tarmac band at
  500 m. The surveyed paving is painted in (`vector_tiles::Survey`,
  `surveyed::raster_survey`) in the colour the meshes give it, averaged over
  the shader's stone pattern (`paving::far_rgb`, pinned to
  `ground_detail.wgsl`), and the OSM ribbons the survey replaces are left out.
  Built land is painted under grass, as the ground stack orders it — a park
  inside a residential area was the residential beige from the air.
- Groningen's street trees, lamps, bins and chargers were all elsewhere: the
  city's GeoServer now answers in Web Mercator unless asked, the reader took
  every coordinate as RD, and the city's register replaces the BGT's trees
  wherever it covers — so the city drew neither (174 registered around
  Linnaeusplein, none drawn). The request names EPSG:28992, a page outside the
  RD grid is refused, and the request is in the cache fingerprint so the
  misplaced cells already stored are never read again. The city's bus shelters
  and traffic signals are read too; `FurnitureKind::TrafficLight` is new,
  appended so the mask bits keep their places.
- Measured walls stood their measured height on top of the walkway: two 2 m
  slabs down the Gorechtvijver's stepped bank, a 4.25 m grey screen along the
  Westerhaven. A measured wall now finds its foot on its lower side, in pieces
  that follow the ground, and atlas gives retaining walls (kademuur, damwand,
  walbescherming) their own `quay` form, drawn flush with the quay.
- Moored boats were draped on the ground like benches, tipped up a sloping
  bank; they are built at the water's surface and placed after the drape. A
  cell over its boat or parked-vehicle cap is thinned evenly instead of
  losing whatever came last.
- The far LoD1.2 blocks were a random terracotta four times in five, so from
  3 km the flat industrial roofs were red. They take the shells' rule: the
  measured roof by BAG id, else flat grey or the era's tile; atlas writes
  `ref:bag` and `start_date` into the blocks for it.
- Colours against the photo: grass 0x6E8A4C → 0x526E44 (a third too bright,
  too yellow), and red brick weathered to (132, 102, 90) in atlas and in the
  client's unmeasured defaults — the Grote Markt was a red carpet beside its
  own taupe photograph.

The atlas half (quay form, block ids, brick colour) shows only after the
`bgt`, `buildings` and `roofs` datasets are re-run.

fix(shots): an aerial reference that covers the frame and survives a bad tile

The camera-matched aerial reference stopped at a fixed 900 m and faded to
haze, so a straight-down capture from 1.5 km came back as a disc in a grey
frame. Its reach is now six camera heights (900 m to 12 km), and the photo is
layered from the camera outwards, each layer at the finest zoom that fits, so
the ground under a low camera is no longer drawn at the horizon's zoom.

One PDOK 502 used to discard the whole reference. Tiles are retried three
times and a tile that still fails is drawn grey; only a mosaic with no tile
at all is an error.

`--dump-state` and `--csv` gain camera_lat/camera_lng/aim_lat/aim_lng, where
the camera actually is and points, read back out of the drawn world. A
`--look-at` carried over from an earlier `--at` aimed a "Grote Markt" shot a
kilometre east, and the requested lat/lng the metrics reported hid it.

test(calls): a stand-in picture whose edges show in a capture

The call screen captures used the stand-in camera's test card, whose
bottom third is black by design, so a video filling the screen read as
one stopping two-thirds down. The --ui call presets now draw a portrait
frame (what an upright phone sends) with a gradient to its edges and a
white border.

feat(calls): a full-screen call screen, laid out like a phone's

The call was a bar at the top of the map with 120 pt tiles, which made
video unusable on a phone. systems::call_screen replaces it, in the
shape Signal and WhatsApp use:

- an incoming call takes the whole screen, Decline red left and Answer
  green right at thumb height; over a call you are in it is a banner;
- in a call the other person's picture fills the screen (letterboxed
  only when an upright phone picture meets a wide desktop window), your
  own is a corner window, a group is a grid with you as a tile, and the
  controls sit on the bottom edge, fading over video after 4 s;
- the arrow or Back folds it to a green bar at the top so the chats and
  the map work during a call (a Back/Escape rung, dismiss::CallScreen),
  and folding never ends a call;
- notices (missed, declined, ended) go on their own after 6 s.

The call buttons take a diameter and wear a frosted plate when on, so
they read over a picture. --ui callincoming|call|callvideo|callgroup|
callfolded seed a stand-in call for scripted captures.
